chronic alcohol treatment of rats and mice may influence their progeny in a way that is similar to the effects of chronic alcohol consumption.
chronic alcoholization of animals may cause biochemical alterations in the functions of monoamine metabolizing enzymes in the progeny of these animals.

In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidation of the mechanisms of genetically determined alcoholic motivational state in offsprings.
elucidation of mechanisms of genetically determined alcoholic behaviour in offsprings and possible prophylaxis.
the mechanisms of genetically determined alcoholism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

chronic ethanol treatment of animals leads to a series of changes in their offsprins, and these changes are not restricted to the somatic and behavioural level, but include also the molecular and genetic ones.

chronic alcohol treatment in parents may cause disturbances in the functions of monoamine-oxidases and c-fos gene which may lead to the appearance of pathological alcoholic motivation in their offspring which were not subjected directly to chronic alcohol treatment.
chronic alcohol treatment may influence functions of genes in progeny of alcohol-treated animals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chronic alcohol treatment may influence the progeny through a complex of mechanisms including biochemical and genetic ones.
chronic alcohol treatment influences functions of genome of offsprings which are not subjected to alcohol.
the offsprings of alcohol-treated animals may develop alcoholic motivation as a result of genetic alterations in functions of monoaminergic system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the offsprings of animals chronically treated with ethanol are more susceptible to the development of pathological alcohol motivation than the progeny of non-chronically treated animals.
the mechanisms of genetically determined alcoholic motivations may be based on disturbances of functions of monoamine-oxidases, and on impairments of genome regulation.
chronic alcohol treatment in parents can influence the progeny, and this influence is mediated by changes in the expression of genes involved in regulation of the alcohol consumption.
